rendered:
The premise does not match the document: the authors did not strain the NiTi wires beyond 10%[1]. The Methods say the coated wires were pulled up to 5%[2] and 10%[3] strains, and state: "Tensile deformations beyond 10% were not[4] performed to avoid delamination of the coating from the wire surface[5]." So higher strains were deliberately avoided because they could peel the V2O5 film off the wire.

The strain levels were chosen for a different reason: the authors wanted the applied strain to exceed the cracking threshold of the films. They wrote: "We chose substrate strains of 5%[6] and 10%, which would sufficiently exceed the saturation crack density[7]" as reported for similar ALD films. The NiTi substrate was strained so that the applied strain was higher than the critical strains needed to crack the films for a given thickness, and the shape-memory behaviour of the alloy then held the film in a locked-in compressive strain after unloading.
